data.title: AI as Normal Technology
data.author: randomwalker
data.article_summary: 本文提出将人工智能（AI）视为“常规技术”的 vision。这种观点并不否认AI的影响，而是将其与那些认为AI会成为独立、超智能实体的乌托邦或反乌托邦观点相对立。作者认为，AI是一种工具，人类应保持对其的控制，且这种控制无需极端政策或技术突破。文章分为四部分：第一部分指出AI的变革性影响将是缓慢的，区分了AI方法、应用和采纳的不同时间尺度；第二部分讨论了在高级AI世界中，人类与AI的分工，强调控制权仍在人类手中；第三部分分析了AI作为常规技术对风险的影响，认为这导致与视AI为类人实体的不同缓解策略；第四部分讨论了对AI政策的启示，主张减少不确定性并强调应对灾难性风险的弹性策略。作者旨在描述AI作为常规技术的中位结果，并拒绝技术决定论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI是否应被视为“普通技术”，以及其未来影响和监管问题

不同观点：
• [roxolotl] 认为，将AI视为“普通但具变革性”的技术是一种中庸且少见的观点。历史上其他变革性技术（如蒸汽动力、电力等）也经历了类似的从热情到怀疑的周期，因此当前对AI的期望应保持历史视角，避免被科幻作品影响。
• [xpe] 对“AI是普通技术”的说法提出质疑，认为该表述混淆了描述、预测和规范三个不同层面的问题。主张不应过早地将这三者捆绑在一起，因为AI领域变化迅速，描述和预测都应保持灵活性。同时批评了Gary Marcus的观点缺乏逻辑一致性。
• [pluto_modadic] 批评当前对大语言模型（LLM）的狂热追求，认为这种发展方向是错误的，且不环保。主张让当前的LLM热潮消退，期待光子计算等新突破，而不是依赖于不断建设数据中心。
• [bux93] 讨论了欧盟AI法案，认为其重点不在AI本身，而是商业流程的质量保证。担心有些人会利用类似文章反对任何形式的监管，即使这些监管对公众有利。
• [lubujackson] 引用了Jeff Bezos关于技术变革的TED演讲，认为AI可能像电力或互联网一样成为重大的范式转变，强调历史经验有助于理解当前的AI发展。
• [sandspar] 认为文章的写作过于复杂，主张可以用更简洁的语言表达相同观点，即“AI本身并不决定未来，社会和机构才是推动者”。
• [xpe]（补充）指出文章未充分讨论军事AI，而这涉及到国际动态和军备竞赛问题，无法简单用“老问题”来概括。
• [bilsbie] 简单提到AI可能像互联网一样，既改变一切又似乎什么都没改变。
• [Nevermark] 赞赏文章的理性立场，但指出技术的缓慢扩散和人类适应问题仍是一个重要挑战，特别是如果AI推动了其他领域的创业潮。
• [anonzzzies] 作为程序员，认为当前的AI工具已经有用，但未来改进无法预知，因此没必要过度思考未来。
• [cootsnuck] 表示文章清晰表达了自己的观点，认为随着AI hype的消退，越来越多的人会接受这种中庸立场。
• [cainxinth] 认为LLM已经融入其日常工作多年，批评了那些过度吹捧或贬低LLM的人，指出LLM虽有缺陷但仍非常有用。
• [iamgopal] 预测小型、快速的AI将像数据库操作一样简单，并会出现由大型LLM引导的专用软件。
• [dakiol] 认为AI只有当开源版本比闭源版本更强大时，才会成为“普通技术”，类似于Linux在操作系统中的地位。
• [gazpacho] 认为AI像Excel/Word一样，虽不需AGI（人工通用智能）就能引发社会变革，特别是如果它导致大量工作岗位流失。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是AI是否应被视为“普通技术”，以及是否应过早对其未来进行规范性讨论。
• 另一个争议点是军事AI的特殊性未被充分讨论，而这一领域涉及国际军备竞赛和复杂的国际关系。
• 对LLM的实用性和当前技术水平的评价存在分歧，一些人认为其非常有用，另一些人则批评其脆弱性和过度炒作。
• 开源与闭源AI技术的未来发展也是一个讨论热点，特别是开源AI在技术普及中的角色。

43697717.article_content:
We articulate a vision of artificial intelligence (AI) as
normal technology
. To view AI as normal is not to understate its impact—even transformative, general-purpose technologies such as electricity and the internet are “normal” in our conception. But it is in contrast to both utopian and dystopian visions of the future of AI which have a common tendency to treat it akin to a separate species, a highly autonomous, potentially superintelligent entity.
1
1. Nick Bostrom. 2012. The superintelligent will: Motivation and instrumental rationality in advanced artificial agents.
Minds and Machines
22, 2 (May 2012), 71–85. https://doi:
10.1007/s11023-012-9281-3
; Nick Bostrom. 2017.
Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies
(reprinted with corrections). Oxford University Press, Oxford, United Kingdom; Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, and Ilya Sutskever. 2023. Governance of Superintelligence (May 2023).
https://openai.com/blog/governance-of-superintelligence
; Shazeda Ahmed et al. 2023.
Building the Epistemic Community of AI Safety
. SSRN: Rochester, NY. doi:
10.2139/ssrn.4641526
.
The statement “AI is normal technology” is three things: a
description
of current AI, a
prediction
about the foreseeable future of AI, and a
prescription
about how we should treat it. We view AI as a tool that we can and should remain in control of, and we argue that this goal does not require drastic policy interventions or technical breakthroughs. We do not think that viewing AI as a humanlike intelligence is currently accurate or useful for understanding its societal impacts, nor is it likely to be in our vision of the future.
2
2. This is different from the question of whether it is helpful for an individual user to conceptualize a specific AI system as a tool as opposed to a human-like entity such as an intern, a co-worker, or a tutor.
The normal technology frame is about the relationship between technology and society. It rejects technological determinism, especially the notion of AI itself as an agent in determining its future. It is guided by lessons from past technological revolutions, such as the slow and uncertain nature of technology adoption and diffusion. It also emphasizes continuity between the past and the future trajectory of AI in terms of societal impact and the role of institutions in shaping this trajectory.
In Part I, we explain why we think that transformative economic and societal impacts will be slow (on the timescale of decades), making a critical distinction between AI methods, AI applications, and AI adoption, arguing that the three happen at different timescales.
In Part II, we discuss a potential division of labor between humans and AI in a world with advanced AI (but not “superintelligent” AI, which we view as incoherent as usually conceptualized). In this world, control is primarily in the hands of people and organizations; indeed, a greater and greater proportion of what people do in their jobs is AI control.
In Part III, we examine the implications of AI as normal technology for AI risks. We analyze accidents, arms races, misuse, and misalignment, and argue that viewing AI as normal technology leads to fundamentally different conclusions about mitigations compared to viewing AI as being humanlike.
Of course, we cannot be certain of our predictions, but we aim to describe what we view as the median outcome. We have not tried to quantify probabilities, but we have tried to make predictions that can tell us whether or not AI is behaving like normal technology.
In Part IV, we discuss the implications for AI policy. We advocate for reducing uncertainty as a first-rate policy goal and resilience as the overarching approach to catastrophic risks. We argue that drastic interventions premised on the difficulty of controlling superintelligent AI will, in fact, make things much worse if AI turns out to be normal technology— the downsides of which will be likely to mirror those of previous technologies that are deployed in capitalistic societies, such as inequality.
3
3. Daron Acemoglu and Simon Johnson. 2023.
Power and Progress: Our Thousand-Year Struggle over Technology and Prosperity
.PublicAffairs, New York, NY.
The world we describe in Part II is one in which AI is far more advanced than it is today. We are not claiming that AI progress—or human progress—will stop at that point. What comes after it? We do not know. Consider this analogy: At the dawn of the first Industrial Revolution, it would have been useful to try to think about what an industrial world would look like and how to prepare for it, but it would have been futile to try to predict electricity or computers. Our exercise here is similar. Since we reject “fast takeoff” scenarios, we do not see it as necessary or useful to envision a world further ahead than we have attempted to. If and when the scenario we describe in Part II materializes, we will be able to better anticipate and prepare for whatever comes next.

data.title: Four Years of Jai (2024)
data.author: xixixao
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了编程语言Jai的优缺点以及作者四年来的使用经验。作者是一位经验丰富的程序员，接触过多种语言和框架，如C、C++、Java、Python和JavaScript等。文章首先回顾了软件性能在硬件快速发展背景下逐渐变差的趋势，原因包括CPU架构变化、脚本语言的流行、以及面向对象编程等方法论的局限性。

Jai语言以其媲美C的性能和现代编程习惯为目标，试图成为C++的强大替代品，同时注重提升程序员的开发体验。作者在2020年加入Jai的Beta测试，并已在专业项目中使用三年。文章从高层次概述、优点、缺点、专业使用、Beta状态和未来发展等多方面进行分析，尽管Jai仍在封闭测试中，作者对其前景持积极态度。

总的来说，Jai在性能和开发体验间取得了较好平衡，但其长期发展仍待观察。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Jai编程语言的特性、开源与否、与其它语言的比较以及实际应用

不同观点：
• [sph] 认为Jai作为封闭源码语言不值得投入学习，特别是在现代不再像90年代那样接受封闭软件。尽管目前处于封闭alpha阶段可以理解，但希望最终能开源或作为自由软件发布。同时关注Jai在系统编程方面的能力，例如是否容易写内核、是否支持内联汇编和自定义链接阶段等。

• [VyseofArcadia] 批评当前软件对硬件性能的浪费，指出在过去10-20年间硬件进化被软件低效抵消。认为行业应更关注效率问题，特别是在应用程序和操作系统层面。

• [TinkersW] 对Jai的开发团队对RAII（资源获取即初始化）机制的理解表示怀疑，并指出C++程序的重建时间不应过长。对Jai的元编程和部分设计选择（如使用字符串表示"sin"/"cos"）感到困惑，认为文章未能清晰展示Jai的优势。

• [mppm] 认为Jai长期处于封闭测试状态令人不解，一方面理解开发者不想被外界干扰，但另一方面这也浪费了关注者的精力和时间，导致知识被逐渐遗忘。

• [sesm] 指出async/await模式在JS中更多是为了代码可读性，而非性能。

• [pcwalton] 回应关于内存安全的讨论，指出如果不想使用垃圾回收，就必须在编译器复杂性或语言限制之间做出权衡，认为不可能存在没有任何缺点的系统。

• [lifthrasiir] 认为Jai的问题在于它像开源语言一样启动却未真正开源，导致困惑和失望。指出许多其他语言在测试阶段仍保持开源，并认为Jai没有实际理由继续保持封闭。

• [kbr-] 质疑Jai通过defer机制取代RAII的可行性，指出在某些情况下（如将需要清理的资源对象放入向量并转让所有权）destructor的重要性。

• [perching_aix] 反问如果将复杂性放入编译器，那么编译器将如何工作，质疑是否存在魔法或 clairvoyance。

• [malkia] 提到Jai的线程上下文栈设计类似GoLang的context，认为这种设计在多线程编程中是必要的。

• [spacechild1] 质疑匿名函数在JS中是否会导致内存分配。

• [phtrivier] 担心在Jai发布时人们可能已经转向Zig或Rust，导致Jai变得 irrelevant，但也希望这种担忧是错误的。

• [IshKebab] 认为Jai难以与Zig竞争。

• [sushidev] 希望文章中有更多代码示例。

• [msmshazan] 关注Jai何时会进入开放测试阶段。

补充讨论：
• Jai的开源状态和其与Zig、Rust的竞争关系是主要争议点。
• 对Jai在系统编程和性能优化方面的能力存在不同看法和期待。
• 部分评论对Jai的特定设计选择（如元编程、字符串表示函数）感到困惑。
• 对内存管理和RAII机制的不同理解和偏好也是讨论的焦点。

Four Years of Jai

2024-12-02
6335 words

Contents
I’ve been programming for long enough to be righteously cantankerous about a lot of things. The list of languages, frameworks and libraries I’ve worked with professionally or on personal projects is too long to list – but it includes everything from C and assembly languages through C++, Pascal and Delphi, through Java and Clojure, through Perl, PHP, Python, Javascript, Typescript and so on. I’ve tinkered with Rust, APL, Uiua, Erlang and Haskell. I’ve been around the block a few times.
So let me just open this discussion by saying: I’ve seen the good, the bad and the ugly, and I know how big the “ugly” category is – how ridiculously small the “good” category is.
Which is why, when I first heard of Jai, I was intrigued. The central focus made sense: a language of comparable performance to C, but with modern idioms, conveniences and tooling – a language aiming to be a powerful alternative to C++ in environments where performance is everything, while emphasizing the importance of programmer morale. This seemed like music to my ears, and I followed the occasional updates for years.
Then, in early 2020, I got invited to join the Beta. From what I could tell I was about the 20th-or-so person to join it.
Now it’s four years in, and further, even though it’s still in closed Beta (I’ll come back to that), I have been using Jai professionally for the last three years – a decision which could be considered controversial, but I’ll address that in this essay.
What I’m going to cover here is:
The high level overview
Things I like
Things I don’t like
Using Jai professionally
The status of the Beta
The road forward
But, this essay will also be 0-indexed:
0. The lost era of good software
Software has been getting slower at a rate roughly equivalent to the rate at which computers are getting faster.
The causes of this are manifold. Some of it is attributable to the maxim that became popular in the 90’s, that software developers were more expensive than faster hardware, so they should be encouraged to not waste their time writing good code if bad code written quickly will suffice.
Part of it is due to architectural changes made to CPUs around 1999, which introduced a layered CPU cache system, broke a lot of assumptions that had held true for decades up until that point. In particular, CPUs and RAM used to have roughly equivalent clock speeds and fetching data from RAM would take 1-2 CPU cycles, so it wasn’t very expensive. But as the clock speeds diverged and RAM grew in size, these diverged – now it can take up to 200 CPU cycles for a memory read to return. As a result, caching is more important than ever, and many things that weren’t bad before, or even actively encouraged, such as linked lists where each item is randomly allocated on the heap, are now insanely expensive.
Some if it is compounded by the development, in particular since the early 90’s, of scripting languages that are meant to be used for everyday software development – the likes of Perl, Ruby, Python, PHP and Javascript. What these brought to the table was a sense of “high level”-ness; that you could write code in a way that was abstracted away from the particulars of the underlying architecture by way of a bytecode interpreter or a virtual machine, or in some cases a just-in-time compiler. This presented many benefits, in particular a reduced need to be concerned with resource management, a task relegated to a garbage collector or such. Suddenly programmers were being encouraged to pretend they knew nothing about the hardware their program was destined to run on. Just assume that resources are abundant, that their allocation and deallocation was practically free, and if things started getting sluggish they could just ask management for more servers.
This came at a cost, but in many cases the efficiency hit was easily justified. Some languages went as far as to make the case that the efficiency tradeoff itself was a feature: that the existence of a virtual machine that hogged memory and reduced your code execution speed made it more “portable”. “Write once, run anywhere,” they claimed, except in practice it was never quite all that.
Some of the slowdown comes due to various ideologies and methodologies, including but not limited to
Object Oriented Programming
, RAII (Resource Allocation Is Initialization) and
Clean Code
having turned out to be conceptual traps which provided a sense of achievement and righteousness, justified by terms like “zero cost abstraction”, “encapsulation” and “cleanliness” which in practice had huge performance hits, and a host of other issues, associated with them.
And some of the slowdown comes because programming paradigms have largely failed to keep up with the rapid expansion from single-core to multi-core and multi-threading. Many of the general purpose concurrency and parallelism models being pushed turn out to have unintuitive performance bott
43699564.article_summary:
本文讨论了编程语言Jai的优缺点以及作者四年来的使用经验。作者是一位经验丰富的程序员，接触过多种语言和框架，如C、C++、Java、Python和JavaScript等。文章首先回顾了软件性能在硬件快速发展背景下逐渐变差的趋势，原因包括CPU架构变化、脚本语言的流行、以及面向对象编程等方法论的局限性。

Jai语言以其媲美C的性能和现代编程习惯为目标，试图成为C++的强大替代品，同时注重提升程序员的开发体验。作者在2020年加入Jai的Beta测试，并已在专业项目中使用三年。文章从高层次概述、优点、缺点、专业使用、Beta状态和未来发展等多方面进行分析，尽管Jai仍在封闭测试中，作者对其前景持积极态度。

总的来说，Jai在性能和开发体验间取得了较好平衡，但其长期发展仍待观察。

data.title: A New ASN.1 API for Python
data.author: woodruffw
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了ASN.1在加密学、网络协议和Python中的重要性及其面临的挑战，并宣布了一个新的ASN.1 API开发计划。ASN.1是一种数据结构描述语法，广泛应用于TLS握手、X.509证书验证、LDAP、SNMP等核心网络协议中。然而，其历史上有许多内存损坏和拒绝服务漏洞。当前Python中的ASN.1库（如pyasn1）性能不足，且容易导致解析差异风险。

为了解决这些问题，一个新的ASN.1 API将集成到PyCA Cryptography中，具备以下特点：
1. **性能**：使用Rust编写，提升解析速度。
2. **减少差异**：与现有X.509 API共享解析器，降低差异风险。
3. **现代化**：采用声明式dataclasses风格接口，支持类型提示。

该项目由Alpha-Omega资助，延续了此前Sovereign Tech Fund支持的X.509路径验证工作，旨在改善Python在加密学和供应链安全方面的生态系统。

43728279.article_content:
If you’ve ever worked with cryptography, PKI schemes, or low-level networking
in Python, you’ve likely encountered
ASN.1
.
ASN.1 undergirds every TLS handshake (via
X.509
path validation),
provides the serialization layer for core internet protocols like
LDAP
,
SNMP
,
and
3GPP
, and generally operates as the
lingua franca
of cryptographic
primitive and protocol representation.
ASN.1’s critical role is complemented by a colorful security history:
implementations of ASN.1’s encoding rules have historically been a
rich source of
memory corruption and denial-of-service vulnerabilities
. Similarly,
ASN.1’s presence at the lowest layers of the internet’s protocols
makes performance and a lack of
parser differentials
a critical requirement.
Python has multiple excellent ASN.1 implementations (like
pyasn1
,
asn1
, and
asn1tools
), but these generally
fall into the latter category: being written purely in Python makes performance
a concern, and integration into a stack where other ASN.1 parsers are used
(e.g., at the X.509 layer) introduces a differential risk.
We’re changing that: with the help of funding from
Alpha-Omega
,
we’re building an ASN.1 API for
PyCA Cryptography
that addresses
three key shortcomings in the Python ecosystem today:
Performance
: This new API will use a
pure Rust ASN.1 parser
,
giving us close-to-native parsing performance.
Differential reduction
: The parser mentioned above is already used
by
PyCA Cryptography
for its X.509 APIs. This will reduce the need for
“mix and match” approaches to ASN.1 parsing, which in turn drive
differential vulnerabilities.
Modernization
: The new API will expose a declarative
dataclasses
style interface replete with type hints, making it familiar, idiomatic,
and compatible with type checkers.
For example, an ASN.1 definition like this:
Doohickies ::= SEQUENCE {
tschotchkes       OCTET STRING,
baubles           INTEGER,
knickknacks       UTF8String,
whatchamacallits  SEQUENCE OF OBJECT IDENTIFIER,
gizmos            SET OF GeneralizedTime OPTIONAL
}
…will correspond to the following Python code:
from
datetime
import
datetime
from
cryptography.hazmat
import
asn1
@asn1.sequence
class
Doohickies
:
tschotchkes
:
bytes
baubles
:
int
knickknacks
:
str
whatchamacallits
:
list
[
asn1
.
ObjectIdentifier
]
gizmos
:
set
[
datetime
]
|
None
doohickies
=
Doohickies
.
from_der
(
b
"..."
)
print
(
doohickies
.
tschotchkes
)
doohickies
.
to_der
()
# b"..."
This work is a logical continuation of our previous work on
X.509 path validation
, as funded by the
Sovereign Tech Fund
. It
reflects our ongoing commitment to improving the Python ecosystem, particularly
in the areas of cryptography and supply chain security.
Please
get in touch
if you’re interested in learning more, or funding
similar work!
Some quick background on ASN.1
ASN.1
, or Abstract Syntax Notation One, is an
interface description language
(IDL). That’s a fancy way of saying that it’s a syntax for describing
data structures in a language- and platform-agnostic manner.
Confusingly, ASN.1 is
not itself
a serialization format. Instead, it defines
encoding rules
, which in turn define serialization and deserialization
of ASN.1 structures in different settings. In practice,
ASN.1 is synonymous
1
with the
Distinguished Encoding Rules
, or DER.
Figure 1: A helpful visual explanation of ASN.1's different encoding rules
We’ll treat “ASN.1” and “DER” as interchangeable for the purposes of this post.
Instead of delving too deeply into the intricacies of both
(
Let’s Encrypt covers them excellently
), we’ll focus on the properties
of DER that have kept it relevant for decades:
DER is a
canonical
encoding:
There’s only one way to encode a given ASN.1
structure in DER. In other words, the encoding of an ASN.1 structure in DER
is deterministic and can be round-tripped while preserving bit-for-bit
equality.
DER is
relatively compact
:
DER defines a binary format and, as a
consequence of being canonical, forbids non-minimal encodings of integers,
booleans, and times.
DER is a
self-describing
and
self-delimiting
encoding:
A given DER
message can be fully and soundly parsed without prior reference to a
schema or format description beyond the encoding rules of DER themselves.
These properties lend themselves naturally to what web developers would
call “progressive enhancement”: an application that consumes DER can
decode the specific structures it cares about while skipping the ones it
doesn’t, decoding only their length in order to jump ahead to the next one.
DER supports
arbitrary-precision integers
:
The
INTEGER
type in DER
is functionally unconstrained in size, which makes it suitable for
representing the kinds of large numbers that regularly appear in
cryptographic settings (e.g., primes).
Put together, these properties make DER very popular in cryptographic,
networking, and telecommunications settings.
More precisely, it’s very popular in the guts of each of these settings:

data.title: The Subjective Charms of Objective-C
data.author: wmlive
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了17世纪博学家莱布尼茨梦想创造一种完美表达所有科学真理的通用语言（characteristica universalis），这一梦想虽未实现，但影响了今天的编程语言。莱布尼茨发明了二进制等，其思想在现代计算机科学中得以延续。作者以自身经历为例，讲述了他对Objective-C语言的特殊情感。尽管这种语言因其冗长和独特语法而备受争议，但在2010年代，它却是开发Mac和iPhone应用的主要工具。作者在大学后期自学Objective-C，通过一本“大黑客牧场”系列书籍掌握了这门语言，并感受到其强大的表达能力。Objective-C源自对象导向编程时代，由Tom Love和Brad Cox创造，因被乔布斯的NeXT公司采用而免于消失，后成为苹果产品核心语言。尽管Objective-C语法复杂，但它提供了一种独特的编程体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Objective-C语言及其相关技术、生态和历史演变

不同观点：
• **赞赏Objective-C的独特设计和贡献**：
  - Objective-C的运行时（runtime）非常出色，特别是在键值编码（KVC）、键值观察（KVO）和绑定（bindings）等机制上的实现非常创新。
  - 自动引用计数（ARC）在没有垃圾回收（GC）的情况下实现了自动内存管理，令人印象深刻。
  - Distributed Objects和XPC等技术非常出色，其他技术难以媲美。

• **与C++的对比**：
  - Objective-C在扩展C语言以实现面向对象方面比C++更优雅和强大，尤其是通过方括号明确传递消息的语义。
  - Objective-C是C的超集，允许调用任何遗留代码或在性能关键部分使用C语法。

• **Objective-C未能广泛流行**：
  - 尽管在NeXT/Apple生态系统外Objective-C并未广泛使用，但其动态特性对用户界面开发非常有益。
  - FOSS社区未广泛采用Objective-C令人遗憾，GTK等工具包尝试模拟消息传递机制。

• **对Swift的看法**：
  - 一些开发者对Swift持保留态度，认为其从多种流行语言中借用特性，导致代码风格不一致。
  - 年轻工程师多被Swift吸引，而非Objective-C的历史和设计。

• **Objective-C在非Apple平台上的困难**：
  - 在Windows上配置Objective-C开发环境非常困难，GNUstep的libobjc2是唯一值得尝试的运行时，但依赖问题复杂。
  - 尝试创建轻量级根类以支持手动引用计数和ARC遇到诸多问题，显示出在Apple生态外使用Objective-C的挑战。

补充讨论：
• **历史背景和演变**：
  - Objective-C的演变与NeXT和Apple的收购及技术发展紧密相关，OpenStep和WebObjects等项目对Objective-C的历史影响深远。
  - 尽管Swift在2014年推出后Objective-C的地位受到挑战，但由于大量遗留代码和性能原因，Objective-C仍有其价值。

• **技术细节和工具支持**：
  - Objective-C的头文件设计使其在使用动态编码工具时非常有效，接口和协议使得实现的重构更加简单。

After inventing calculus,
actuarial tables, and the mechanical calculator and coining the phrase “best of all possible worlds,” Gottfried Leibniz still felt his life’s work was incomplete. Since boyhood, the 17th-century polymath had dreamed of creating what he called a
characteristica universalis
—a language that perfectly represented all scientific truths and would render making new discoveries as easy as writing grammatically correct sentences. This “alphabet of human thought” would leave no room for falsehoods or ambiguity, and Leibniz would work on it until the end of his life.
A version of Leibniz’s dream lives on today in programming languages. They don’t represent the totality of the physical and philosophical universe, but instead, the next best thing—the ever-flipping ones and zeroes that make up a computer’s internal state (binary, another Leibniz invention). Computer scientists brave or crazy enough to build new languages chase their own
characteristica universalis
, a system that could allow developers to write code so expressive that it leaves no dark corners for bugs to hide and so self-evident that comments, documentation, and unit tests become unnecessary.
But expressiveness, of course, is as much about personal taste as it is information theory. For me, just as listening to
Countdown to Ecstasy
as a teenager cemented a lifelong affinity for Steely Dan, my taste in programming languages was shaped the most by the first one I learned on my own—Objective-C.
To argue that Objective-C resembles a metaphysically divine language, or even a good language, is like saying Shakespeare is best appreciated in pig latin. Objective-C is, at best, polarizing. Ridiculed for its unrelenting verbosity and peculiar square brackets, it is used only for building Mac and iPhone apps and would have faded into obscurity in the early 1990s had it not been for an unlikely quirk of history. Nevertheless, in my time working as a software engineer in San Francisco in the early 2010s, I repeatedly found myself at dive bars in SoMa or in the comments of HackerNews defending its most cumbersome design choices.
Objective-C came to me when I needed it most. I was a rising college senior and had discovered an interest in computer science too late to major in it. As an adult old enough to drink, I watched teenagers run circles around me in entry-level software engineering classes. Smartphones were just starting to proliferate, but I realized my school didn’t offer any mobile development classes—I had found a niche. I learned Objective-C that summer from a cowboy-themed book series titled
The Big Nerd Ranch
. The first time I wrote code on a big screen and saw it light up pixels on the small screen in my hand, I fell hard for Objective-C. It made me feel the intoxicating power of unlimited self-expression and let me believe I could create whatever I might imagine. I had stumbled across a truly universal language and loved everything about it—until I didn’t.
Twist of Fate
Objective-C came up in the frenzied early days of the object-oriented programming era, and by all accounts, it should have never survived past it. By the 1980s, software projects had grown too large for one person, or even one team, to develop alone. To make collaboration easier, Xerox PARC computer scientist Alan Kay had created object-oriented programming—a paradigm that organized code into reusable “objects” that interact by sending each other “messages.” For instance, a programmer could build a Timer object that could receive messages like start, stop, and readTime. These objects could then be reused across different software programs. In the 1980s, excitement about object-oriented programming was so high that a new language was coming out every few months, and computer scientists argued that we were on the precipice of a “
software industrial revolution
.”
In 1983, Tom Love and Brad Cox, software engineers at International Telephone & Telegraph, combined object-oriented programming with the popular, readable syntax of C programming language to create Objective-C. The pair started a short-lived company to license the language and sell libraries of objects, and before it went belly up they landed the client that would save their creation from falling into obscurity: NeXT, the computer firm Steve Jobs founded after his ouster from Apple. When Jobs triumphantly returned to Apple in 1997, he brought NeXT's operating system—and Objective-C—with him. For the next 17 years, Cox and Love's creation would power the products of the most influential technology company in the world.
I became acquainted with Objective-C a decade and a half later. I saw how objects and messages take on a sentence-like structure, punctuated by square brackets, like [self.timer increaseByNumberOfSeconds:60]. These were not curt, Hemingwayesque sentences, but long, floral, Proustian ones, syntactically complex and evoking vivid imagery with functio

data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: 本文总结了relax-pk项目在约束系统方面的进展。在阶段2初期，团队对如何处理约束系统存在不确定性。虽然约束系统具有很大潜力，但以往存在不可靠的问题，如“浮动性”（一个参数变化导致其他参数不自然漂移）、“崩溃”（系统部分操作导致其他部分失稳）和性能不佳。为了解决这些问题，Alex通过传播已知信息和利用线性关系（如y=mx+b）减少了求解器需要处理的变量数量，从而提高了系统的稳定性和性能。团队还引入了“聚类”技术，将约束和变量分组独立求解，提高了收敛速度并为并行化处理提供了可能。最终，多个不稳定结构在新系统中表现稳定，并尝试了多种求解器以优化性能，包括uncmin和g9项目中的改进版。团队计划未来探索更多高性能求解器选项。

43729932.article_content:
title
Constraint System
dated
Fall 2023
author
Summary of work on relax-pk
At the beginning of phase 2, we weren’t sure what to do about constraints. Based on past exploration, constraints seemed to hold a lot of promise but were notoriously unreliable. A good constraint system could unify and power a number of key aspects of the dynamic medium we seek. It would allow for mechanical constructions, like a rope and pulley, that feel physically correct. It would allow for a computational model that bridged between algebraic formulae and tangible objects, like an architectural drawing that changed in response to edits in a parameter table. It’d allow for true bidirectional computation, instead of the limited / biased computation we had in Crosscut.
But constraint systems are hard to implement. They tend to suffer from the following issues:
“Floaty-ness”, where manipulating one parameter causes other parameters to drift in ways that feel unnatural or unrealistic.
“Blow-ups”, where manipulating part of the system causes other parts of the system to collapse inward or explode out to infinity (divergence toward or away from zero, rather than convergence on a reasonable value).
Poor performance, either due to slow convergence or to excess recalculation when constraints are added or removed.
Early in this phase Alex was optimistic that with a bit of effort these issues could be overcome. After a few weeks he was able to show very promising results. This early success built on his earlier work on [
propagation of knowns
] to reduce the number of variables whose values had to be determined by the solver. Then, by leveraging equality constraints (and more generally, any linear relationship between variables —
y=mx+b
where
m
is not zero) he further reduced the number of dimensions that the solver had to worry about.
As an example, consider an angle constraint that “exports” two variables: one whose value is the angle in degrees, and another whose value is in radians. While either or both of those variables may be referenced by other constraints or scrubbed by the user, they collapse to a single variable as far as the solver is concerned — after all, once you know the value of one of them, you can compute the value of the other.
This technique is not just an optimization that enables the solver to converge to a solution more quickly; it often enables the solver to find a solution where it wouldn’t have been able to otherwise. It also improves the feel of our prototype by eliminating the “floaty-ness” that results from duplicated state. More importantly, this technique also enabled us to avoid blow-ups when duplicated or “uneven” constraints are added to a model.
To illustrate this point, suppose the user has added an angle constraint between points
A
and
B
, which introduced a variable
θ
AB
. Now consider what happens when the user adds another angle constraint that involves the same points, but this time in the opposite direction. This is a situation that could lead to an unstable construction. Our new constraint system detects this, and instead of adding the second angle constraint, it introduces the variable
θ
BA
and a linear relationship
θ
BA
= θ
AB
+ π
. So nothing changes for the solver: there is still only one variable (
θ
AB
) to solve for, and only one constraint to satisfy. But to the user, it looks like there are two separate angle constraints. They can further constrain
θ
BA
, or later remove the second angle constraint if they wish. (We are happy to report that all of the
unstable constructions we documented in phase 1
are perfectly stable in our new constraint system.)
Another useful technique we developed for the constraint system is what we call “clustering”, i.e., the partitioning of the constraints and the variables on which they operate into
clusters
that can be solved independently. (As Avi pointed out, this is analogous to the notion of
simulation islands
in some physics engines.) By breaking up the solver’s workload into clusters, we reduced the number of dimensions it has to worry about, which has led to significant improvements in convergence. Clustering also opens up the possibility for us to parallelize the solver — this is something we can explore when we start to build larger projects/models that require better performance.
While these analyses and techniques are an important part of our constraint system, they are not tied to a particular choice of solver. This gives us the freedom to plug in better options as they become available. In addition to Alex’s relaxation-based solver, we tried several gradient descent-based solvers, which resulted in better convergence. The first was the uncmin from
numericjs
. Later, we found a version of uncmin that was modified by Guillermo Webster for his
g9
project, which gave us even better results. We hope to eventually try @Avi Bryant 's new solver which uses auto-diff (instead of numerical differentiation) and WebAssembly for added performance and stability

• [cedws] 认为WASM和WIT的文档和术语不够清晰，导致在实际操作中遇到很多问题。他特别提到在构建基本模块时，遇到了需要使用libc的情况，增加了复杂性，并希望有更多的博客或资源来解释这些概念。

• [fuhsnn] 对Wasm内在函数作为高层次固定大小SIMD抽象表示感兴趣，并讨论了其在AOT目标中与库如simd-everywhere结合使用的潜力。他还提到string.h中缺少strstr()函数，并提供了一个替代算法的链接。

• [phickey] 对通过提交更改到上游来加快wasi-libc的速度表示支持，认为这是一种良好的改进方法。

• [forrestthewoods] 对SWAR（SIMD within a register）的概念不了解，提出了基础知识方面的疑问。

• [nu11ptr] 对WASM在多种使用场景中的潜力表示乐观，包括客户端浏览器多语言小程序、服务器端多语言小服务程序、以及语言互操作/外部函数接口（FFI）。他特别指出WASI标准化在解决库调用和调用约定问题上的重要性。

补充讨论：
• WASM和相关工具链（如WIT）的复杂性及文档不足的问题被[cedws]提出，表明需要更多的教育资源和简化。
• [fuhsnn] 和 [phickey] 更关注WASM在性能优化和特定技术实现上的潜力，如SIMD抽象和wasi-libc改进。
• [nu11ptr] 提出WASM在解决跨语言互操作性问题的潜力，尤其是在标准化调用约定和库调用方面，预示着WASM在未来多语言环境中的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 目前关于WASM工具和库的文档和术语复杂性是[cedws]提出的一个主要问题，其他讨论者尚未直接回应这一点，但指出了WASM在不同技术层面的潜力和改进方向。

data.title: How a yacht works: sailboat physics and design
data.author: stass
data.article_summary: 本文概述了翼型、帆船和游艇的空气动力学和工作原理，涵盖升力来源、工程公式、动量理论、升力线理论、环流理论等。讨论了翼、鳍和帆的工作原理，涉及展弦比、洗流、平面形状、边界层、雷诺数等概念。还探讨了风洞实验、下洗、升力槽效应、表观风、风梯度对帆扭曲的影响，以及大船仪器仪表的设置。此外，讨论了附件设计、箔片形状、湿表面积和船体设计，包括摩擦阻力、波阻和弧线设计等。最后，分析了船的整体平衡、稳定性、环境影响和规则效应，以及调校技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：帆船运动中的不同兴趣方向、技术应用、市场机会以及设计目标

不同观点：
• **[jp57]** 认为帆船运动可以分为竞赛和巡航两个不同的类别，竞赛者更关注性能优化，如帆 trim 的细节和特殊帆的使用。而巡航者只需要掌握基本的帆船操作技巧即可享受航行。这表明了两种不同兴趣方向的差异。
• **[serkandurusoy]** 提出目前在休闲帆船中现代科技的应用较少，并质疑市场规模是否不足以吸引创业公司进入该领域，希望获得关于创业想法的反馈。
• **[stass]** 强调了技术资源的重要性，推荐了一个专注于帆和船体设计的网站，认为该网站对于对帆性能建模或游艇设计感兴趣的人是非常宝贵的资源。
• **[WALoeIII]** 提到 Arvel Gentry 的研究对帆船空气动力学的影响，推荐了一系列杂志文章，认为这些文章对理解帆船技术非常有帮助。
• **[mendeza]** 对弦乐器的物理原理表示兴趣，并希望学习相关知识以设计自己的乐器，这与其他讨论的帆船技术主题不同。
• **[lasermatts]** 分享了在旧金山学习帆船的资源，并提到了一所提供造船课程的学校，表明对帆船实践学习的兴趣。
• **[reddit_clone]** 希望看到关于帆船运作的动画解释，以更好地理解帆船技术，特别是对于历史帆船的背景知识。
• **[Zeetah]** 表示对帆船的了解有限，但希望通过志愿服务和课程学习获得经验，这反映了新手对进入帆船领域的需求。
• **[mlhpdx]** 指出帆船技术的现代化，特别是新材料和制造技术带来的变化，如上升到平面的船体设计和箔片的广泛使用，强调帆船技术的发展。
• **[boat34189]** 推荐了一个关于大船设计和工程的视频资源，扩展了讨论的范围，包括中型船只的相关性。
• **[contingencies]** 强调了不同帆船设计目标的差异，特别是巡航船和竞赛船在存储空间、居住空间、稳定性等方面的不同需求，并讨论了多体船的设计优势和成本问题。

补充讨论：
• **市场机会**：[serkandurusoy] 提出的关于现代科技在休闲帆船中的应用机会和市场规模的问题，引发了对帆船技术创业的思考。
• **设计目标**：[contingencies] 详细讨论了不同帆船设计目标的优先级，如巡航船的存储空间、稳定性，以及多体船的功能优势和成本问题。
• **文化背景**：[contingencies] 还提供了关于“catamaran”一词的文化历史背景，增加了讨论的深度和趣味性。

争议焦点：
• **竞赛与巡航的差异**：[jp57] 强调竞赛者和巡航者之间的兴趣差异，暗示两者在技术关注点上的不同，而[contingencies] 则通过讨论不同设计目标进一步扩展了这一争议。

data.title: Show HN: Attune - Build and publish APT repositories in seconds
data.author: ilikebits
data.article_summary: Attune 是一个开源的软件制品注册工具，主要用于安全地发布和托管 Linux 软件包，支持 APT 仓库（Debian 和 Ubuntu）。其特点包括灵活部署（自托管或使用托管云基础设施）、安全设计（CLI 本地签署仓库索引，无需暴露签名密钥）和高效性能（增量更新仓库索引）。基本使用步骤包括设置后端服务、安装 CLI、创建和配置软件仓库、添加.deb包、使用GPG密钥签署并部署仓库。该项目采用 Apache-2.0 许可证，主要使用 Rust、Go 和 PLpgSQL 编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于工具 "attune" 的使用和其与类似工具的比较，特别是在管理软件库和发布软件包方面的功能和易用性。

不同观点：
• [yjftsjthsd-h] 认为文档中的命令对没有经验的用户来说可能过于复杂，特别是对于一些参数（如 `-r`, `-c`）没有足够清晰的解释。他还对 URI 的作用和如何与服务器同步提出了疑问。
• [pabs3] 提供了 Debian wiki 的更多选项链接，并提到已将 Attune 添加到列表中，为用户提供更多参考资料。
• [Hackbraten] 质疑 Attune 与 aptly 的区别，尤其是当用户已经拥有对象存储时，是否有必要使用 Attune。
• [benwilber0] 认为 apt 仓库只是 web 根目录中的文件，并提到 Debian 生态系统中有许多脚本来生成和维护这些目录。他对仅提供托管 .deb 文件和索引更新的价值表示怀疑。
• [frabona] 比较了 Attune 和 mise/ubi，表示对解决初始摩擦感兴趣，并希望进一步讨论。
• [3np] 表示对未来支持其他发行版/仓库的功能有兴趣，特别是希望有一个统一的接口来同步发布多个发行版的软件包。
• [powerawq103846] 简单表达了对该工具的赞赏。
• [jauntywundrkind] 对 Rust 实现表示赞赏，并分享了自己使用 reprepo 的经验，指出配置和发布软件包的效率问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是 Attune 的易用性和文档的清晰度，特别是对于没有相关经验的用户。
• 另一个讨论点是 Attune 与其他类似工具（如 aptly, mise, ubi）的区别和优势。
• 用户对多发行版支持和统一发布接口的需求较为明显，显示出对跨平台解决方案的期待。
• 对配置和部署的简便性也有讨论，特别是与现有工具和方法的比较。

Attune
Attune is a tool for securely publishing and hosting Linux packages.
Flexible deployment:
Deploy a self-hosted package repository, or use our managed cloud infrastructure.
Secure by design:
Attune's CLI does repository index signing locally, so you can own your signing keys without ever exposing them.
Really, really fast:
Attune does incremental repository index rebuilds, so adding and removing packages is really fast.
We currently support publishing APT (Debian and Ubuntu) repositories, with more
coming soon
.
Quick Start
Here's how to set up an APT repository in about 5 minutes.
Requirements
Docker (
docker
)
GnuPG (
gpg
)
Setup
#
############# First, we need to set up the Attune backend.
#
1. Clone the repository.
git clone git@github.com:attunehq/attune.git
&&
cd
attune
#
2. Set up environment variables by copying from .env.example. You should
#
modify these values as needed to suit your deployment, especially
#
ATTUNE_SECRET.
cp .env.example .env
#
3. Start the control plane and supporting services.
docker compose up -d
#
############# Now, we'll install the CLI and set up a repository.
#
4. Install the Attune CLI by downloading it from GitHub Releases.
#
5. Create a repository.
attune repo create -u
'
http://localhost:9000/debian
'
-d bookworm
#
6. Prepare a `.deb` package to host. One way you can do this is by downloading
#
a sample package e.g. `https://cdn.teleport.dev/teleport_17.4.4_arm64.deb`.
#
7. Add the package to the repository
attune repo pkg -r 1 add -c stable/v17
~
/Downloads/teleport_17.4.4_arm64.deb
#
############# Lastly, we'll use a GPG key to sign and deploy the repository.
#
8. If needed, generate a GPG key.
gpg --generate-key
#
9. Get the key ID of the secret key you'd like to use to sign.
gpg --list-secret-keys
#
10. Export your signing key (replace $KEYID with your key ID, which is the 40
#
character string next to the `sec` entries in each key).
gpg --armor --export-secret-keys --output demo-key.asc
$KEYID
#
11. Sign and deploy the repository.
attune repo -r 1 sync -k demo-key.asc
#
############# Congratulations, you're done!
For more detailed setup instructions and configuration options, refer to the
user guide
.

• [jauntywundrkind] 对 Rust 实现表示赞赏，并分享了自己使用 reprepo 的经验，指出配置和发布软件包的效率问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是 Attune 的易用性和文档的清晰度，特别是对于没有相关经验的用户。

data.title: The most famous carbon dioxide absorber
data.author: bemmu
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了1970年阿波罗13号登月任务及其意外情况。阿波罗13号原计划是第三次载人登月，但飞行途中发生爆炸，三名宇航员被困在距地球20万英里的太空中。事故后，他们的生存依赖于利用飞船内的有限材料制作二氧化碳吸收器。文章还介绍了阿波罗计划中的飞船结构，包括指挥舱、服务舱和登月舱。按计划，两个宇航员会使用登月舱降落在月球表面并进行探索，但阿波罗13号因事故未能实现登月。最终，宇航员们通过 ingenuity 和团队合作安全返回地球。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apollo 13故事及其相关技术细节，CO2吸收器，技术兼容性问题以及文化趣闻。

不同观点：
• [londons_explore] 提出是否存在家用CO2吸收器，以将室内CO2浓度降至前工业时代水平（约200ppm），而不是城市房屋中常见的800ppm。该评论关注环保和室内空气质量问题。
• [teekert] 认为Apollo 13的故事引人入胜，并建议将其作为“医疗保健互操作性”演讲的引子。此评论侧重于故事的启发性和应用潜力。
• [breakyerself] 指出文章中关于降落伞减速的描述有误，认为应该是热盾首先通过大气层减速。该评论关注技术细节的准确性。
• [userbinator] 提醒大家这是1960年代的技术，暗示不应以现代标准苛求当时的技术水平。此评论强调历史背景的重要性。

补充讨论：

Unless you are an anaesthetist, you probably wouldn’t know what a carbon dioxide absorber is (red arrow below).
However, for a brief period in the year 1970, carbon dioxide absorbers were what everyone was talking about. This is the story of Apollo 13 which blasted off in 1970 towards the Moon. However, things did not go according to plan and an explosion in the spacecraft left three astronauts stranded 200,000 miles from home. Suddenly this story became headline news. The whole world got to know how the astronaut’s survival depended on whether they could make a carbon dioxide absorber using the limited materials available in their spacecraft.
On July 21, 1969, Neil Armstrong stepped off the ladder of his spacecraft and became the first human to walk on the Moon. The first words spoken by him on the Moon that day are still remembered.
The first lunar landing was part of a series of space missions of the Apollo Space program. On April 11, 1970, it was the turn of Apollo 13 to lift off. This was going to be the third team to land on the Moon. The three astronauts (Lovell, Swigert, and Haise) for this mission were sitting on a massive rocket that would take them into outer space. The rocket (Saturn V), shown below, was about 110 meters tall (360 feet), had a diameter of about 10 meters (33 feet) and weighed about 3,000,000 kilograms (6,500,000 pounds). To appreciate the size of this mammoth rocket, compare its height with the man standing near it (tip of the red arrow).
If you are superstitious and believe that the number 13 is not lucky, then you will be forgiven for thinking that the launch time was rather “unlucky”. Apollo 13 launched at 13:13 ( North American Central Time Zone ).
The image shows the gigantic rocket launching into space.
Within one minute of lift-off, the rocket was travelling at the speed of sound. The rocket was built of various sections and as it went up into space, to avoid carrying unnecessary weight, it was designed to discard sections of itself that were no longer of any use (e.g. parts containing empty fuel tanks). Below is an image of a rocket throwing away a part of itself as it made its way to outer space. These massive pieces fell into the sea ( hopefully not hitting any fishermen below !).
Within about 15 minutes the astronauts reached outer space and started orbiting around Earth. Their orbiting spaceship would have looked like this.
The “spaceship” actually consisted of three parts. These parts will be briefly explained to you so that you will later better understand the drama that took place in this mission.
Let us begin with the “command module “. This is a rather cramped compartment (shown in green below) in which the three astronauts mostly travelled inside.
The command module was attached to a large section called the “service module “. This had an engine to take the astronauts towards the moon and back again towards Earth. Importantly, the service module also provided life-sustaining functions for the astronauts, such as giving oxygen, water and electricity.
The service module had tanks of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen. It also had special devices called “fuel cells”. These fuel cells were able to take hydrogen and oxygen from the tanks to produce water and electricity.
Here is a picture of an actual fuel cell.
So you can see that the service module provides vital supplies of oxygen, water, and electricity for the astronauts sitting in the command module.
Here is an actual picture of a command module and service module attached together.
The third part of the “spaceship” is the lunar module.
The lunar module is used to descend to the Moon, and of course, return back up as well. You will understand the role of the lunar module and the other parts better if I briefly describe to you how a typical Moon mission is expected to happen. Please note that Apollo 13 had a mishap and could not do what is described below. However, by understanding what should have happened, you will better understand the drama that happened.
So, if things went according to plan, the spaceship, with its three main components, would have arrived at the Moon and orbited around it.
Two of the astronauts would move into the lunar module. Unfortunately, one unlucky astronaut would have to remain back in the command module to look after it.
The lunar module, with the two happy astronauts, separates from the command module and descends onto the Moon.
Once safely down on the Moon, they would prepare to get out and explore the surface.
The astronauts would get into their space suits and venture out of the lunar module.
Many missions even took along a “car” to explore greater distances.
After the two astronauts would have enjoyed exploring the Moon, they’d get back into the lunar module. This has a small engine that blasts them away from the Moon.

data.title: College Towns: Urbanism from a Past Era
data.author: toomuchtodo
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了大学城镇（College Towns）的都市化特点及其在现代城市规划中的意义。作者Ryan Allen是南加州一所大学的教授，他通过其新闻通讯《College Towns》探讨高等教育与城市化的交集。文章指出，大学无意中保存了可步行的“战前”社区，这些社区在其他地方多已被拆除以扩建郊区。同时，大学面临高等教育行业的挑战，如博士毕业生就业市场萎缩。此外，文章还提到“城镇与学袍”的冲突，即当地居民反对学生住房，尽管他们选择住在校园附近。Ryan呼吁城市规划者应共同应对停滞和无限制的郊区扩展，而不是仅仅与反对者对抗。文章还讽刺了迪士尼乐园以130美元的费用展示曾经在每个美国城镇自然存在的步行主街。Ryan强调了大学与社区融合的重要性，并通过公共写作和YIMBY主义（Yes In My Backyard）推动这一理念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同文化背景下的城市设计与生活习惯差异，以及大学城与城市规划的关系

不同观点：
• [xixixao] 认为波多黎各的海滩上播放 loud music 是当地文化的一部分，但对于外来者（如欧洲人）来说，这种行为破坏了海滩的宁静氛围。同时，他指出美国城市和欧洲城市在设计上（为车 vs 为行人）的差异，不仅是地理大小的原因，更是文化与建筑历史的结果，这种改变需要很长时间。

• [janalsncm] 讨论住房政策问题，指出由于少数人的反对（“vocal minority”），好的住房政策难以实施，特别是在大学城和加州等地。如果不为住房进行规划，实际上就是在为无家可归者做规划。

• [davidjama] 质疑人们在大学毕业后从适合步行的大学城搬到郊区生活，认为这是一种倒退，因为大学城内短距离步行、高容量的住房以及经济实惠的环境更有利于社会协作与生活。

• [nluken] 认为直接将Zoom访谈的录音转为文字内容会影响可读性，强调播客形式和书面形式的不同需求。

• [bentt] 提出大学或学院往往成为经济利益的渠道，吸引学生的同时也带来商业机会，且美国自由派文化往往伴随着对“不良事物”的严格规则，尤其在旧城保护方面。

• [m463] 认为大学城是人为规划的环境，人口高度同质化，且许多人愿意放弃某些自由。这种控制和统一性使得大学城与普通城市有所不同。

• [bbqfog] 以自身经验指出，大学城由于人口流动性大，住房等基础设施常常破旧不堪，尤其是面对大量年轻人聚会活动时，住房压力更大。

• [kjkjadksj] 认为大学城之所以运转良好，主要是因为学生经济状况和生活方式的特殊性。大多数学生不带车，住在校园附近，形成了一种特殊的通勤和生活模式。这种模式在普通城市中难以复制。

补充讨论：
• [cyberax] 以讽刺口吻提到过去的城市设计（如 bunk beds 和 flophouses）可能成为未来趋势，暗示当前对城市规划的讨论可能忽视了一些历史经验。

• [rtollert] 对某个文本的准确性提出质疑，特别是关于某大学名称的错误使用，认为这暴露了作者对美国大学系统缺乏基本了解，显示出“巨大的红旗”。

争议焦点：
• 文化差异（如音乐习惯、城市设计）是否可以通过政策或时间改变。
• 大学城的规划是否适用于更广泛的城市环境，特别是毕业后从步行友好的大学城搬到汽车依赖的郊区是否合理。
• 住房政策和城市规划中如何平衡短期利益与长期社会福祉。

Today, I bring you an interview with Ryan Allen. Ryan Allen is a professor of international education at University of America in Southern California and the author of the newsletter "College Towns," which explores the intersection of higher education and urbanism. Our conversation covers his transition from academic publishing to public writing, the challenges facing higher education, and how colleges can better integrate with their communities through thoughtful urban design.
College Towns
College Towns, where urbanism meets higher education.
By Ryan M Allen
Key points:
The PhD trap:
"We probably got to start telling people don't go do PhDs" — the job market has collapsed while universities keep churning out graduates destined for precarious employment.
Universities as urban saviors:
Colleges preserved walkable "pre-war" neighborhoods that would have been bulldozed for suburban sprawl elsewhere.
Everyone loves universities except their neighbors:
The persistent "town and gown" conflict sees locals fighting against student housing despite choosing to live near campuses.
The common enemy isn't people—it's stagnation:
Rather than fighting "NIMBYs," urbanists should unite against "freezing towns in amber and endless sprawl."
Disney's $130 urbanism irony:
Disneyland charges visitors to experience the walkable main streets that once existed naturally in every American town before suburban development destroyed them.
Introduction & Background
Dave Deek:
Hi Ryan, how are you doing?
Ryan Allen:
Dave, doing well. Doing all right. It's not quite a sunny day here in Southern California, so I think I've been lied to with that PR campaign.
Dave Deek:
At least it's not Houston where the weather just kind of been bipolar like it's hot and what you imagine Houston to be then it's suddenly cold and rainy and then go back to hot.
Ryan Allen:
Sure. Yeah. I know we Southern Californians shouldn't complain, but we certainly do a lot.
Dave Deek:
All right. But before we dive in, could you share what led you to write College Towns and what's your personal connection to both higher education and urbanism and YIMBYism?
Ryan Allen:
Yeah, sure. I mean, the short story is I received tenure over the summer and I always said once I did get tenure, I was going to try to put more... I'm a professor. I guess I should say that I'm a professor at University of America here in Southern California. I teach international education. And I've always thought that academic publishing is just not very fast. I just had an article that came out a couple days ago that literally it's five years in the making and it just gets bogged down with—I mean peer review is good, but other ways around the sort of the journal system isn't good. The book publishing can be very slow in academic presses.
So I just told myself if I get tenure, I'm gonna start kind of putting myself more out there, writing quickly because it's really hard to get things out there quickly in academia. So I was like, "All right, I can kind of do this myself." So that's kind of the quick story.
I think the longer story is I've always had kind of this passion for public intellectuals or sort of public writing. I mean, I thought maybe at one time I would be a journalist. I had a fork in the road moment of going to a PhD or going to be sort of a journalist with a publication in China. I decided to go do my PhD and even my undergrad background was PR communications which is not really in my area now but it's kind of helped me think about writing and presenting myself.
And then even when I told myself I was going to start College Towns I was hesitant. I think I started in October and I received tenure kind of over the summer. So it's a few months of me just kind of thinking should I really do this? Should I try to write op-eds in popular publications? And I did that. I started kind of trying to publish op-eds in newspapers, magazines, whatever it was and I had two rejections right in a row and I was just kind of annoyed. I was like, "Man, two different rejections, two different articles, two things I wanted to get out there" and it was one of those things like you write it and then as time goes on it can't really be published again. This is kind of a waste of time.
I'm going to keep putting in all this effort and then the things don't get published. So I said, what, I'm just going to start this urbanism and sort of education together. And I love the idea of college towns. I'm passionate about higher ed, but just the college itself.
43729609.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了大学城镇（College Towns）的都市化特点及其在现代城市规划中的意义。作者Ryan Allen是南加州一所大学的教授，他通过其新闻通讯《College Towns》探讨高等教育与城市化的交集。文章指出，大学无意中保存了可步行的“战前”社区，这些社区在其他地方多已被拆除以扩建郊区。同时，大学面临高等教育行业的挑战，如博士毕业生就业市场萎缩。此外，文章还提到“城镇与学袍”的冲突，即当地居民反对学生住房，尽管他们选择住在校园附近。Ryan呼吁城市规划者应共同应对停滞和无限制的郊区扩展，而不是仅仅与反对者对抗。文章还讽刺了迪士尼乐园以130美元的费用展示曾经在每个美国城镇自然存在的步行主街。Ryan强调了大学与社区融合的重要性，并通过公共写作和YIMBY主义（Yes In My Backyard）推动这一理念。
43729609.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同文化背景下的城市设计与生活习惯差异，以及大学城与城市规划的关系

不同观点：
• [xixixao] 认为波多黎各的海滩上播放 loud music 是当地文化的一部分，但对于外来者（如欧洲人）来说，这种行为破坏了海滩的宁静氛围。同时，他指出美国城市和欧洲城市在设计上（为车 vs 为行人）的差异，不仅是地理大小的原因，更是文化与建筑历史的结果，这种改变需要很长时间。

• [janalsncm] 讨论住房政策问题，指出由于少数人的反对（“vocal minority”），好的住房政策难以实施，特别是在大学城和加州等地。如果不为住房进行规划，实际上就是在为无家可归者做规划。

• [davidjama] 质疑人们在大学毕业后从适合步行的大学城搬到郊区生活，认为这是一种倒退，因为大学城内短距离步行、高容量的住房以及经济实惠的环境更有利于社会协作与生活。

• [nluken] 认为直接将Zoom访谈的录音转为文字内容会影响可读性，强调播客形式和书面形式的不同需求。

• [bentt] 提出大学或学院往往成为经济利益的渠道，吸引学生的同时也带来商业机会，且美国自由派文化往往伴随着对“不良事物”的严格规则，尤其在旧城保护方面。

• [m463] 认为大学城是人为规划的环境，人口高度同质化，且许多人愿意放弃某些自由。这种控制和统一性使得大学城与普通城市有所不同。

• [bbqfog] 以自身经验指出，大学城由于人口流动性大，住房等基础设施常常破旧不堪，尤其是面对大量年轻人聚会活动时，住房压力更大。

• [kjkjadksj] 认为大学城之所以运转良好，主要是因为学生经济状况和生活方式的特殊性。大多数学生不带车，住在校园附近，形成了一种特殊的通勤和生活模式。这种模式在普通城市中难以复制。

补充讨论：
• [cyberax] 以讽刺口吻提到过去的城市设计（如 bunk beds 和 flophouses）可能成为未来趋势，暗示当前对城市规划的讨论可能忽视了一些历史经验。

• [rtollert] 对某个文本的准确性提出质疑，特别是关于某大学名称的错误使用，认为这暴露了作者对美国大学系统缺乏基本了解，显示出“巨大的红旗”。

争议焦点：
• 文化差异（如音乐习惯、城市设计）是否可以通过政策或时间改变。
• 大学城的规划是否适用于更广泛的城市环境，特别是毕业后从步行友好的大学城搬到汽车依赖的郊区是否合理。
• 住房政策和城市规划中如何平衡短期利益与长期社会福祉。

data.article_summary: 该页面提供了有关YouTube的各种信息和资源。包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻、版权声明、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者相关条款、隐私政策、安全政策等内容。此外，页面还提及了YouTube的新功能测试、NFL Sunday Ticket服务，以及版权所属信息（2025年，Google LLC）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LTE物联网设备的技术细节、定价与市场定位、远程编程与固件更新、功耗与供电方案

不同观点：
• audunw认为，文章未提及LTE系统级芯片（SoC）的细节，对于很多潜在用户而言，了解所用的芯片是重要的，即使应用中对硬件进行了抽象。
• flyingcircus3反对远程编程功能，认为这仅是针对业余爱好者的噱头。在大规模或小规模部署中，直接在现场设备上修改代码是不可靠的，容易引发版本控制和代码验证问题。更好的做法是在受控环境中开发和测试，然后通过无线更新部署到所有设备。
• RickS对产品的定价和订阅模式表示担忧，认为未公开的价格和潜在的订阅费用是“红旗”。他指出，AI功能的成本如果转嫁给用户，可能降低产品的吸引力。此外，他希望看到明确的价格和限制信息，以便消费者能够提前过滤掉不适合自己的选项。
• usg7关注设备的功耗问题，特别是在电力资源匮乏的地方，询问是否有针对LTE设备的太阳能供电方案或未来计划。
• 999900000999分享了尝试制作LTE太阳能电话的失败经验，指出LTE的经济性和地域差异（多种LTE类型）使得这种设备难以实现。

补充讨论：
• h1t35h对某个“一致性响应问题”提出了疑问，询问是否每次响应不同或不可靠，并建议尝试调节温度或使用特定优化的SQL模型。
• brk分享了一个相关模块的链接，表示这些模块设计精良，可能与讨论中的设备类似。
• hakaneskici询问开发者套件是否已经开始交付，显示出对产品上市进度的关注。
• klinquist建议增加GPS功能，认为这对远程遥测应用非常有帮助。

争议焦点：
• 远程编程的可行性与风险：flyingcircus3认为远程编程风险高，而潜在用户可能认为这是一个实用功能。
• 产品的定价与订阅模式：RickS对未公开的价格和潜在的订阅费用表示不满，认为这影响了消费者的购买决策。

data.title: Understanding the Origins and the Evolution of Vi and Vim
data.author: amosjyng
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了Vi和Vim文本编辑器的起源与演变。Vi和Vim的历史与开源软件的发展密切相关。文章回顾了重要的历史事件和人物，如Vi编辑器的起源可以追溯到1973年英国首个UNIX系统在伦敦玛丽女王大学的安装，以及乔治·库洛里斯（George Coulouris）教授在此开发的“em”编辑器。Vi则是比尔·乔伊（Bill Joy）在加州大学伯克利分校基于“ed”和“em”开发的全屏视觉模式编辑器。Vi和其前身“ex”共享代码，Vi本质上是“ex”的视觉模式。后来，Vi演变为Vim，由布莱姆·米尔纳（Bram Moolenaar）创建，并成为广泛使用的文本编辑器。文章还提及了布莱姆的逝世及其对编辑器历史的反思。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Vi文本编辑器的设计及其历史渊源，以及其在现代编辑器中的地位和影响。

不同观点：
• [qsort] 认为Vi设计极其出色，即使是Busybox中的精简版Vi也比大多数现代IDE功能强大。尽管他喜欢Jetbrains的IDE，但Vim插件对他来说不可或缺。
• [CalChris] 提出TECO才是所有编辑器的鼻祖，尽管TECO是Emacs的直接祖先，而Vi的历史渊源没有直接证据表明与TECO相关。他仍然认为TECO是"ur editor"。
• [sunshine-o] 表示Vi和UNIX shell是美丽的工具，即使在现代高科技环境下仍然被广泛使用，并预测Vi可能会在未来50年内继续拥有用户。
• [bsdz] 分享了他在网络延迟严重的情况下使用Vi键绑定的经验，认为Vi在这种情况下非常高效，类似于Bill Joy在低速调制解调器环境下开发Vi的经历。

补充讨论：
• [nickandbro] 提到他正在开发一个名为Vimgolf.ai的项目，旨在让学习Vim变得更有趣。
• [ggm] 补充了nvi和neovim等其他Vi变种，特别是nvi在BSD中的应用及其在UTF处理上的改进。
• [Animats] 指出RAND编辑器是所有全屏终端编辑器的祖先，具备超前于时代的功能，如分屏编辑和剪贴功能。
• [bodyfour] 纠正了关于Minix选择文本编辑器的历史事实，指出Minix在2013年转向了BSD nvi。
• [jiehong] 和 [jasperry] 提到了Amiga平台上的Vi和Emacs变种，如Bram的Vim最初是为Amiga开发的。
• [kjellsbells] 提到EDLIN，这是MS-DOS上的行编辑器，与UNIX的ed有相似之处。
• [notorandit] 分享了他从1986年起使用Vi的个人经历，并对Emacs持批评态度。
• [patrickdavey] 对文章未提及neovim感到意外。
• [drbig] 提到了CygnusED和ARexx，希望ARexx的核心思想能更广泛地流行。
• [agumonkey] 建议阅读关于ed、TECO等早期非全屏编辑器的历史，认为这也有重要的历史价值。

争议焦点：
• Vi和Emacs的历史渊源及其优劣对比是隐含的争议点，特别是在[CalChris]和[notorandit]的评论中有所体现。
• 关于Minix选择编辑器的历史事实也有一定的纠正和讨论，[bodyfour]指出了相关错误。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 对Vi在现代技术环境下的持续使用和其未来生命力的预测。
• 个人使用Vi的经验分享，如在网络延迟和高科技环境下的高效使用。
• 对Vi和其变种（如nvi、neovim）的技术细节和历史背景的补充。

43691020.article_content:
Understanding the Origins and the Evolution of Vi & Vim
The history of both
Vi & Vim
goes hand in hand with the history of open-source software itself. This article is a trip back to the origins of UNIX text editors. Let's look at the important players and historical events that shaped their evolution.
Gustavo Pezzi
11 August 2023 · 15 min read
I went to East London last week to visit my wife's alma mater,
Queen Mary University
. As I stopped to grab a cup of coffee, I received a message saying that
Bram Moolenaar
, the creator of Vim, had passed.
To be honest, with a new family member keeping me busy at home, and a new course on MIPS assembler that I'm recording for
my school
, I am finding very difficult to keep up with the latest news. So, I confess that I received the news of Bram's passing almost a week too late.
I did not know Bram personally and I am far from being a Vim
connoisseur,
but the fact that I was visiting Queen Mary University forced me to stop for a moment and reflect on how that place was connected to the long and vibrant history of Vim.
Queen Mary University had an important role in the history of the Vim editor. It was here that, in 1973, the first UNIX system of the UK was installed, and it was also here that professor
George Coulouris
developed an editor called
em
. The creation of
em
ended up snowballing into the development of
vi
and many other
vi clones
after that.
Queen Mary University of London
, where George Coulouris taught in 1976.
Ed
The UNIX shell is extremely text-heavy. Executables are invoked via text, parameters are passed via text, streams of data flow up and down the system via text, and virtually everything in the OS shell is done with tokens of text. It is no surprise that UNIX users are so passionate about text editors.
We should probably start with
ed
, which was a command-line editor created by Ken Thompson designed to work well with
teleprinters
rather than display terminals.
Teletype Model 15 teleprinter.
Ed is what we call a
line editor.
Editing one line at a time made perfect sense for
teleprinters,
but with the popularity of video displays taking over, most users found frustrating having to work with
ed.
That included Queen Mary's George Coulouris, who considered
ed's
commands to be cryptic and not suitable for
"mortals".
Ed (line) editor.
Ken Thompson's
ed
was inspired by another editor called
QED
(quick editor). QED was also a line-oriented editor for teleprinters developed for the
SDS 940 console
. Ken Thompson rewrote QED using
BCPL
to run on
MULTICS
(the precursor to UNIX).
Fun fact
: Ed became the defacto line-mode editor for UNIX, and it remains a part of the
POSIX
standard to this very day. After all,
"Ed is the standard text editor"
.
Em
Following a series of frustrations with
ed,
in February of 1976, while acting as a lecturer at Queen Mary College, Coulouris decided to enhance
ed
using Ken Thompson's original source code as a starting point. That's how the editor
em
(Ed for Mortals)
came to be.
Coulouris'
em
was designed to work well with display terminals. It was a single-line-at-a-time visual editor, and it was also one of the first programs on UNIX to make heavy use of
"raw terminal input mode",
in which the running program (rather than the terminal device driver) handled all keystrokes.
But George Coulouris was not the only one disappointed with
ed.
Across the pond, more people were getting frustrating working with Ken Thompson's line editor
Vi
When Thompson visited
UC Berkeley
in 1976, he brough with him a broken Pascal compiler for UNIX that needed to be fixed.
Bill Joy
, a student from UC Berkeley, was in charge of fixing Thompson's Pascal system. As days passed, Joy noticed that
ed
was holding him back.
UC Berkeley
, where Bill Joy was a graduate student when he developed
vi.
In the summer of 1976, when George Coulouris visited UC Berkeley, he brought a
DECtape
containing
em
and showed it to various people at the university. Some considered this new type of text editor to be a resource hog, while others, including Bill Joy, were impressed with Coulouris' program.
Bill Joy was a graduate student at UC Berkeley and wrote the
vi
text editor.
Inspired by Coulouris'
em,
and by their own tweaks to Ken Thompson's
ed,
Bill Joy and Chuck Haley (both graduate students at UC Berkeley) created a new editor called
en.
Soon after, they "extended" the
en
editor and created
ex
. In October of 1977, Bill Joy added a full-screen visual mode to
ex,
which came to be
vi
.
The
vi
editor is able to render and edit text in full-screen mode.
Both
vi
and
ex
share their code. You can think of
vi
as launching
ex
with an extra parameter to enable the capability to render and edit the text onto a computer display terminal. In reality,
vi
is basically
ex's visual mode
.
The name "vi" comes from the abbreviated ex command (vi) to enter the visual mode from within the editor. Later, as most of us probably know,
vi
became the actual executable name that we invoke from the

data.title: 15,000 lines of verified cryptography now in Python
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
2022年11月，有人在Python的GitHub仓库中提交了issue 99108，建议在SHA3实现中出现CVE后，Python应为其所有哈希相关基础设施采用经过验证的代码。截至最近，该问题已解决，Python默认暴露的所有哈希和HMAC算法现在都由经过验证的加密库HACL*提供。这次过渡对Python用户完全透明，没有功能损失。Python现在包含来自HACL*的15,000行经过验证的C代码。从上游HACL*仓库拉取新版本已实现自动化。HACL*成功实现了新功能，如Blake2算法的附加模式、覆盖所有Keccak变体的SHA3新API、严格的抽象模式以处理构建系统困难、适当的错误管理（特别是分配失败），以及利用HMAC算法实例化HACL的通用“流”功能，包括需要同时保持两个哈希状态的优化。

这一成果历时2.5年，Aymeric Fromherz贡献巨大，他承担了大量实施工作。Son Ho早期贡献关键，将HACL的“流”功能泛化以处理需要“预输入”的块算法，这对实现优化的HMAC至关重要。在Python方面，Gregory P. Smith、Bénédikt Tran和Chris Eibl提供了大量帮助。HACS系列研讨会建立了联系并提供了动力。

流式API复杂且难以实现，因为它们处理具有复杂不变性的长期状态。参考实现中的SHA3在2022年受到CVE影响，Python也因此受到牵连。流式API允许输入任意长度数据，并处理缓冲和中间哈希计算。完全通用的验证通过依赖类型捕捉块算法的定义，并一次验证通用流构造，然后应用于具体算法以生成流API。

实现完全泛型需要处理许多细节，如最终摘要长度是否固定、块算法是否需要预输入等。

In November 2022, I opened
issue 99108
on
Pythonâs GitHub repository, arguing that after a recent CVE in its implementation of
SHA3, Python should embrace verified code for all of its hash-related infrastructure.
As of last week, this issue is now closed, and every single hash and HMAC algorithm exposed by
default in Python is now provided by
HACL*
, the
verified cryptographic library. There was no loss of functionality, and the transition was entirely
transparent for Python users. Python now vendors (includes in its repository) 15,000 lines of
verified C code from HACL*. Pulling newer versions from the upstream HACL* repository
is entirely automated and is done by invoking a script. HACL* was able to successfully implement
new features to meet all of the requirements of Python, such as: additional modes for the Blake2
family of algorithms, a new API for SHA3 that covers all Keccak variants, strict abstraction
patterns to deal with build system difficulties, proper error management (notably, allocation
failures), and instantiating HACLâs generic âstreamingâ functionality with the HMAC algorithm,
including an optimization that requires keeping two hash states at once.
This is the culmination of 2.5 years of work, and could not have happened without the invaluable
help of
Aymeric Fromherz
, who shouldered a lot of the
implementation burden.
Son Ho
had a key contribution early on, generalizing
HACLâs âstreamingâ functionality to be able to handle block algorithms that require a âpre-inputâ.
This slightly obscure generalization was actually essential to implement a suitable, optimized HMAC
that keeps two hash states under the hood. On the Python side, Gregory P. Smith, BÃ©nÃ©dikt Tran, and
later Chris Eibl were big champions and provided a lot of help. Finally, the HACS series of
workshops created connections (hello, Paul Kehrer!) and provided sufficient momentum to make this
happen. A warm thank you to both the Python and verified cryptographic communities!
As I oftentimes like to do, Iâll provide a little bit of a look behind the scenes, and comment on
some of the more interesting technical aspects that are too low-level for a research paper.
A Primer on Streaming APIs
Many cryptographic algorithms are
block
algorithms, meaning that they assume their input is
provided block by block, with special treatment for the first and last blocks. Well-known block
algorithms include hash algorithms, MAC algorithms (e.g. Poly1305, HMAC), and more. In practice, the
block API is not user-friendly: rarely does one have the data already chunked in blocks;
furthermore, computing a result (e.g., a hash) invalidates the state of the block algorithm, which
makes e.g. computing the intermediary hashes of the TLS transcript difficult.
For these reasons, cryptographic libraries typically expose
streaming
APIs, meaning clients can
provide inputs of any length; the library then takes care of buffering the input, flushing the
buffer as soon as a full block is obtained. A streaming API typically also allows extracting
intermediary hashes without invalidating the state.
Streaming APIs are hard, because they manipulate long-lived state with complex invariants: the
(unverified) reference implementation of SHA3 was hit with a
bad
CVE
in 2022, which Python âinheritedâ, because it
vendored that very same SHA3 implementation.
Streaming APIs are hard also because the
underlying block algorithms differ in a myriad of different ways: all hash algorithms accept an
empty final block,
except
for Blake2; some need to retain the key at run-time (Poly1305), some can discard it
after initialization (HMAC, optimized); some need some initial input before processing the key
(Blake2), some donât; and so on.
Given this inherent complexity, streaming algorithms are a good candidate for verification: we wrote
a
research paper
in 2021 about this very problem.
Fully generic verification
The main idea from the paper is that one can capture, using dependent types, what a block algorithm
is
. Once thatâs done, it suffices to author and verify a generic streaming construction once and
for all over an abstract definition of block algorithms. Then, just like you instantiate a template
in C++, you apply the generic streaming construction to a concrete block API and voilÃ  â a
streaming API for that one block algorithm, âfor freeâ.
The fist hitch is that thereâs quite a big delta between what we presented in the paper (Listing
12), and
what actually lives in the
repository
.
Specifically, capturing
any
block algorithm requires a lot of genericity.
The user may or may not specify the length of the final digest â for instance,
each SHA3 hash has a fixed output length, but the Shake variants produce a result whose length is
user-provided.
The block algorithm may expect to receive a pre-input before the blocks of data. For e.g. SHA2,
the pre-input is empty, but for Blake2 in keyed hash mode, the pre-input is the key block.

data.title: Judge Rules Blanket Search of Cell Tower Data Unconstitutional
data.author: bradac56
data.article_summary: 美国内华达州一名法官裁定，执法部门从手机信号塔获取大量个人数据的“塔数据转储”行为违反了第四修正案，该修正案保护公民免受非法搜查和扣押。尽管如此，法官仍允许警方在当前案件中使用通过这种非法搜查获得的证据，因为警方是基于善意申请的搜查令。这起案件涉及一名叫Cory Spurlock的男子，他被指控与贩卖大麻和雇凶杀人有关。尽管搜查令被判定为普遍搜查且不符合宪法，但由于是首次遇到此类问题，证据不予排除。此类裁定可能最终会上诉至最高法院，以做出最终裁决。此前，2018年的**Carpenter v. United States**案中，最高法院曾裁定警方未经 warrant 获取手机定位数据属违宪，但未明确界定“塔数据转储”的合法性。

Judge Rules Blanket Search of Cell Tower Data Unconstitutional
Matthew Gault
·
Apr 18, 2025
at 9:00 AM
Judge says tower dumps violate the 4th amendment, but will let the cops do it this one time, as a treat.
A cell tower amongst the trees. Image:
Wikideas1
via Wikimedia Commons.
This article was produced in collaboration
with Court Watch
, an independent outlet that unearths overlooked court records.
Subscribe to them here
.
A judge in Nevada has ruled that “tower dumps”—the law enforcement practice of grabbing vast troves of private personal data from cell towers—is unconstitutional. The judge also ruled that the cops could, this one time, still use the evidence they obtained through this unconstitutional search.
Cell towers record the location of phones near them about every seven seconds. When the cops request a tower dump, they ask a telecom for the numbers and personal information of every single phone connected to a tower during a set time period. Depending on the area, these tower dumps can return tens of thousands of numbers.
Cops have been able to sift through this data to solve crimes. But tower dumps are also a massive privacy violation that flies in the face of the Fourth Amendment, which protects people from unlawful search and seizure. When the cops get a tower dump they’re not just searching and seizing the data of a suspected criminal, they’re sifting through the information of everyone who was in the location.
A Nevada man, Cory Spurlock, is facing charges related to dealing marijuana and a murder-for-hire scheme. Cops used a tower dump to connect his cellphone with the location of some of the crimes he is accused of. Spurlock’s lawyers argued that the tower dump was an unconstitutional search and that the evidence obtained during it should not be. The cops got a warrant to conduct the tower dump but argued it wasn’t technically a “search” and therefore wasn’t subject to the Fourth Amendment.
U.S. District Juste Miranda M. Du rejected this argument, but wouldn’t suppress the evidence. “The Court finds that a tower dump is a search and the warrant law enforcement used to get it is a general warrant forbidden under the Fourth Amendment,” she said in a ruling filed on April 11. “That said, because the Court appears to be the first court within the Ninth Circuit to reach this conclusion and the good faith exception otherwise applies, the Court will not order any evidence suppressed.”
Du argued that the officers acted in good faith when they filed the warrant and that they didn’t know the search was unconstitutional when they conducted it. According to Du, the warrant wasn’t unconstitutional when a judge issued it.
Du’s ruling is the first time the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit has ruled on the constitutionality of tower dumps, but this isn’t the first time a federal judge has weighed in. One in Mississippi
came to the same conclusion
in February. A few weeks later, the Department of Justice
appealed the ruling
.
There’s a decent chance that one of these cases will wind its way up to the Supreme Court and that SCOTUS will have to make a ruling about tower dumps. The last time the issue was in front of them, they kicked the can back to the lower courts.
In 2018, the Supreme Court considered
Carpenter v. United States
, a case where the FBI used cell phone location data to investigate a series of robberies. The Court decided that law enforcement agencies violate the Fourth Amendment when they ask for cell phone location data without a warrant. But the ruling was narrow and the Court declined to rule on the issue of tower dumps.
According to the court records for Spurlock’s case, the tower dump that caught him captured the private data of 1,686 users. An expert who testified before the court about the dump noted that “the wireless company users whose phones showed up in the tower dump data did not opt in to sharing their location with their wireless provider, and indeed, could not opt out from appearing in the type of records received in response to [the] warrant.”

data.title: Loglan'82: programming language for object-oriented and distributed programming
data.author: danielam
data.article_summary: Loglan'82是一种专为对象和分布式编程设计的编程语言，具有独特的安全高效对象管理系统。它支持类模块、协同程序模块和线程模块（进程），允许创建类对象、协同对象（含纤程）和进程对象（含线程）。Loglan的虚拟机可以通过互联网连接成一个虚拟的多处理器计算机，实现程序计算在处理器间的分布。它采用统一模型处理并发和分布式计算，减少学习成本。Loglan'82提供了一个原创的"alien call"通信与同步协议，支持线程间方法调用。该语言解决了诸如静态链接、类嵌套与继承、对象安全释放、垃圾回收效率等研究问题。它适用于有抱负的程序员、教学以及科研人员，并提供了Linux和Windows平台的编译器。

• [guenthert] 对语言的现代性发表看法，提到该语言的一些特性比MODULA-2更为现代，但对当今存在的大量编程语言表示感慨。同时，对类的前缀使用与当代的派生概念进行了类比。

Loglan'82 project
Z Lem
Skocz do:
nawigacji
,
wyszukiwania
Loglan'82 is a programming language conceived for object and distributed programming.
It has many features that make Loglan'82 a tool surpassing other programming languages:
It enjoys a unique safe and efficient system of managing objects, see
Safe dealocation
,
It offers modules of classes (
class
), moreover it allows to declare modules of cooperating objects i.e.
coroutines
and modules of threads (
process
). One can create not only objects of classes, but also objects of coroutines with their
fibres
and objects of processes, aka agents with their
threads
.
Virtual machines of Loglan may connect (through internet) in a virtual, multiprocesorr computer.This allows to distribute a computation of a program between processors in a controlled way.
Objects of processes (agents) can be alocated on different nodes of a network of virtual machines or on the same machine. It means that Loglan uses one model for concurrent as well as for distributed computations. (Less learning).
Loglan'82 offers an original, fully object protocol of communication and synchronization, so called
alien call
of methods of an agent.
Each object of a process, i.e. an agent may create its own system of coroutine objects and manage it,
there are other interesting and useful features of Loglan'82. Try to discover them!
We are hoping that the information contained on these pages will be of interest to:
Ambitious programmers
-- for the language  Loglan'82 offers a couple of constructs and solutions not known in other programming languages:
Should you manage the memory of objects and to avoid the dangerous phenomenon of
dangling pointers
? Try the instruction
kill
.
Should the software you are creating use concurrent, or distributed computations, or a combination of these two models -- choose Loglan'82. For it offers one model of all these variants of non-sequential computations. In this way you will diminish the cost of programming.
Please take time to learn about the
alien call protocol
. It is an original invention of our collaborator Bolek Ciesielski. It is fully object way of calling methods of a thread A from another thread B.
For those who are creating quasi-concurrent computations (by fibres) we are offering a richer version of classes i.e.
coroutines
.
Teachers
-- Loglan'82 is a good choice:
if you aim to present all tools and methods of object oriented programming and to avoid passing from one to another programming language when need arises to illustrate a subsequent tool of object programming,
if you wish to construct a larger project that contains specification of data structures (classes), implementation of specifications and the verification of the implementation with respect to the specification.
Researchers
-- for the language incorporates the results of scientific research  of a few non-trivial problems:
is it possible combine two methods of creation of program modules: nesting and inheritance? Before we agreed to admit nesting and inheritance we had to answer a couple of fundamental questions:
How to assure static linking between an applicative occurrrence of an identifier and a proper occurrence of a declaration of this identifier?
How to determine the direct superclass of a given class?
Is it possible to extend a class by a function (a procedure)?
Does the management of object necessarily leads to the phenomenon of dangling references?
How effective can be garbage collection?
Is it possible to deallocate no longer needed objects in a safe and effective way?
How to define the semantics of coroutines in a consistent way?

data.title: UML diagram for the DDD example in Evans' book
data.author: takaakit
data.article_summary: 该项目通过UML图展示了Eric Evans书中DDD（领域驱动设计） cargo运输系统的结构与行为，基于GitHub的dddsample-core项目源码创建。UML图帮助理解DDD战略和战术设计及系统运作机制。主要内容包括：用户与系统的交互序列图、域模型概览类图、特定货物对象图、系统总体结构图以及多个行为场景的通信图（如系统初始化、货物跟踪、货物预订和路线分配）。此外，还提供了 Booking 和 Transport 两个上下文的有向图。要查看详细属性和操作，需使用Astah Professional/UML工具打开模型文件。参考Evans的《Domain-Driven Design》一书可深入理解DDD理论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：UML（统一建模语言）的应用、优缺点以及替代方案

不同观点：
• **neilv** 认为UML在系统建模和沟通中仍然具有重要价值，但错误可能很难发现，尤其是在不熟悉领域的情况下。错误的图表可能导致严重后果，如大量返工、项目放弃或技术债务。此外，UML不应被视为仅用于销售展示的“市场架构”。
• **BerislavLopac** 提出C4模型比UML更适合系统架构文档，因为C4模型在符号和组件建模上更加灵活，并推荐了工具IcePanel。
• **andrewstuart** 认为UML曾一度主导企业IT，但幸运的是它并没有成为未来。隐含的观点是UML已经过时。
• **alganet** 认为好的UML是简单且部分的，强调简化图表和跳过团队已知的信息。此外，优秀的UML是“无UML”，即代码本身已经足够清晰。UML图表应该是可抛弃的，长期保存作为文档是一个错误。
• **stevoski** 通过一个案例说明了领域专家在UML图表沟通中的潜在误解，强调了在实际使用中可能出现的意外情况。
• **ak_111** 好奇UML的现状，指出其曾在企业计算中无处不在，但现在似乎消失了，询问其是否像SOAP和Java Applets一样过时，以及什么替代了它。
• **firesteelrain** 认为如果理解符号和关系，UML图表非常有意义，并提到经常与非技术人员使用这些图表。
• **throw_m239339** 认为UML在传达架构方面是有用的，但因为一些厂商滥用“快速UML开发”导致开发者对UML产生反感。同时指出UML非常老旧且面向Java面向对象编程，但序列图仍在使用。
• **karlgkk** 提到AI模型已经能够将PDF或文档转换为UML，虽然还不是完美，但可以节省时间。

补充讨论：
• UML的价值和应用场景存在争议，部分人认为其在现代开发中已经过时，而另一些人则认为在特定情况下仍然有用。
• C4模型和其他工具被提及作为UML的替代方案，尤其是在灵活性和易用性方面。
• 讨论中提到了UML在沟通和实际使用中的潜在问题，如领域专家的理解误差和技术债务。
• 现代技术（如AI模型）对UML图表生成的影响也被提及，显示出技术进步对传统工具的潜在替代。

UML Diagram for the DDD Example in Evans' Book
This project uses UML diagrams to illustrate the structure and behavior of the DDD example—a cargo shipping system—from Eric Evans' book (
Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software
). These diagrams are created based on the source code of the
dddsample-core
project on GitHub. The diagrams aim to help us understand how the example implements the strategic and tactical designs of DDD and the mechanisms by which it operates.
If you want to get into DDD theory, check out Evans' book. If you want to get into the implementation details, check out the source code of the dddsample-core project. Also, if you want to understand the UML model behind these diagrams, open the model file (ddd-example-in-evans-book.asta) using the modeling tool
Astah Professional/UML/Viewer
.
Clicking on the UML diagram image below opens it in Diagram Map
*1
.
*1
: Diagram Map allows you to zoom and pan, like Google Maps, when viewing a UML diagram. You can view it with any browser. To create one on your own,
Astah Professional/UML
and the
m+ plug-in
are required.
User-system interaction
This sequence diagram illustrates the key interactions between the user and the system, with references to other diagrams.
Domain model overview
This class diagram illustrates the basic elements of the domain model and their relationships. The layout of the domain model elements is based on the diagram presented in the dddsample-core project. Attributes and operations are hidden to focus on understanding the elements and their relationships. If you want to see them, open the model file (ddd-example-in-evans-book.asta) using the modeling tool Astah.
Domain objects for "ABC123" cargo
This object diagram shows the basic domain objects and thier connections. In particular, it shows the object snapshot associated with the cargo object "ABC123," which is preset as sample data. The cargo "ABC123," which is en route from HongKong to Helsinki, is currently at the port of New York, where unloading has been completed.
Overall structure
This class diagram illustrates the overall structure of the cargo shipping system: it is composed of two contexts, the Booking context and the Transport network context. The system is implemented using Spring projects such as Spring Boot / MVC / Data JPA. Note that this diagram focuses on elements and relationships that may be considered and does not reflect the entire implementation. Attributes and operations are also hidden to focus on understanding the elements and their relationships. If you want to see them, open the model file (ddd-example-in-evans-book.asta) using the modeling tool Astah.
Behavior 1: Initialization
This communication diagram illustrates a scenario in which the user launches the cargo shipping system, with a focus on messages that may be worth considering.
Behavior 2: Cargo tracking
This communication diagram shows a scenario in which the user requests tracking for cargo "ABC123" on the cargo tracking page. The cargo "ABC123," which is preset by the system and en route from HongKong to Helsinki, is currently at the port of New York, where unloading has been completed.
Behavior 3-1: Cargo booking
This communication diagram shows a scenario in which the user registers new cargo on the cargo booking page. The new cargo is set to be shipped from New York to Helsinki.
Behavior 3-2: Route suggestion
This communication diagram illustrates a scenario in which the user requests cargo routing on the cargo booking result page, followed by the presentation of route candidates.
Behavior 3-3: Route assignment
This communication diagram illustrates a scenario in which the user requests to assign new cargo to a delivery route on the route selection page.
Extra: Directed graph
This is a directed graph
*2
that represents the structural elements and their relationships, associated with the Booking context and the Transport network context. This graph allows you to view the element relationships in various layouts.
*2
: To create this directed graph on your own,
Astah Professional/UML
and the
m+ plug-in
are required.

43731250.article_summary: 该项目通过UML图展示了Eric Evans书中DDD（领域驱动设计） cargo运输系统的结构与行为，基于GitHub的dddsample-core项目源码创建。UML图帮助理解DDD战略和战术设计及系统运作机制。主要内容包括：用户与系统的交互序列图、域模型概览类图、特定货物对象图、系统总体结构图以及多个行为场景的通信图（如系统初始化、货物跟踪、货物预订和路线分配）。此外，还提供了 Booking 和 Transport 两个上下文的有向图。要查看详细属性和操作，需使用Astah Professional/UML工具打开模型文件。参考Evans的《Domain-Driven Design》一书可深入理解DDD理论。

不同观点：
• **neilv** 认为UML在系统建模和沟通中仍然具有重要价值，但错误可能很难发现，尤其是在不熟悉领域的情况下。错误的图表可能导致严重后果，如大量返工、项目放弃或技术债务。此外，UML不应被视为仅用于销售展示的“市场架构”。

data.author: jprohov
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了在地壳深处发现的微生物，这些“地下生物”正在改变科学家对生命及其演化的理解。传统观念认为生命依赖阳光和氧气，但这些微生物无需阳光，通过呼吸诸如铀和砷等元素生存，甚至帮助清理人类产生的有毒污染物。它们生活极其缓慢，可能数十万年才更换所有分子，有些甚至存活百万年之久。这些发现挑战了生命生存条件的传统界限，提示我们需要重新思考达尔文的进化论。在能量极其有限的环境中，这些微生物的演化方式与地表生物截然不同，提出了关于生命本质和进化的新问题。
